research_question: Does explainable source-quality-based selection produce a better and/or more efficient domain-specific RAG knowledge base than an equivalent random-source baseline?

frozen_baseline.status: FROZEN - not modified by this experiment; ground truth remains agent-authored, human review pending
frozen_baseline.ground_truth_caveat: All experiment results inherit the baseline limitation: ground truth was agent-authored by reading indexed chunk texts and is NOT human-reviewed. Results are NOT publication-grade.

hypothesis.H1_quality: Corpora whose sources are selected by the existing explainable source-quality score answer more benchmark questions correctly at equal or smaller corpus size (higher Recall@K / MRR at equal N).
hypothesis.H2_efficiency: Quality-selected corpora reach equal retrieval quality with fewer chunks / fewer characters (more efficient) than random selection.
hypothesis.H0_null: No difference between strategies beyond selection noise.

independent_variable: Source-selection strategy: QUALITY_SELECTED (top-N by existing SourceQualityScorer score) vs RANDOM_BASELINE (uniform random N from the same pool, fixed seed).

controlled_variables.vector_database: Qdrant 1.19.1, cosine, one collection per KB
controlled_variables.evaluation: frozen benchmark questions only, strict mode (allow_keyword_fallback=false)
controlled_variables.domain_analysis: deterministic dev-mock analyzer (no LLM key configured); identical DomainSpec content across all runs, so relevance scoring is stable

dependent_variables: Recall@3, Recall@5, Recall@10 (chunk basis, explicit GT only)
question coverage: share of benchmark questions whose ground-truth chunk exists in the corpus (reported separately, never mixed into retrieval metrics)
efficiency: documents, chunks, corpus character count, ingest wall-time, index wall-time

candidate_pool.note: All URLs verified reachable (HTTP 200) on 2026-09-15 before freezing. The 11 baseline-corpus URLs are included so N=11 can reproduce the baseline corpus composition when quality-selection picks them.

strategies.QUALITY_SELECTED: Rank the pool by the persisted source-quality score (existing signals/weights, real accessibility probes, deterministic mock DomainSpec relevance). Take the top N. Ties broken by URL ascending.
strategies.RANDOM_BASELINE: Uniform random sample of N URLs from the same pool using Python random.Random with the fixed seed below. Same pool ordering as quality ranking input.

evaluation_protocol.ground_truth_translation: Re-chunking regenerates chunk IDs, so the frozen benchmark's expected_chunk_ids are translated to each experimental corpus via deterministic chunk content_hash (identical chunker config => identical chunk text => identical hash). The benchmark file itself is never modified. Per-run translation stats are recorded.
evaluation_protocol.coverage_rule: A question is ANSWERABLE in a corpus iff at least one of its expected chunk content-hashes exists there. Only answerable questions are scored; excluded questions are listed per run. Coverage is reported separately and is NOT a retrieval metric.
evaluation_protocol.metrics: Recall@K, Precision@K, MRR, NDCG@K (binary) from the existing evaluator, strict mode only.
evaluation_protocol.repetitions: 1 (single fixed seed; repeated-seed variance is future work and a stated limitation)
